title.narrative: Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment

description.narrative: The project aims to support the poor and most vulnerable of the population by providing targeted interventions to provide job opportunities now, improve access to better jobs for tomorrow and build resilience. The project will achieve this through the following three components using a multi-sectoral approach: Component 1 (Connecting Youth and Women to Better Jobs Today) will support youth and women's access wage and self-employment activities in selected urban areas. Component 2 (Investing in People for Better Jobs Tomorrow) aims to directly support vulnerable households, comprising three subcomponents designed to address different aspects of human capital development and resilience through cash transfers. Sub-component 2.1 will support the provision of a unconditional cash transfers; sub-component 2.2 will provide human capital co-responsibility cash transfers for health and nutrition as well as education; and sub-component 2.3 will provide financing of emergency cash transfers in response to a potential future climate-related shock and establish a contingent funding mechanism. Component 3 (Adaptive Social Protection Delivery Systems and Project Management) supports three key areas crucial for the long-term sustainability and effectiveness of social protection interventions in Somalia. Sub-component 3.1 supports institutional capacity building for adaptive social protection systems; sub-component 3.2 finances a National Socio-economic Survey for the Unified Social Registry; and sub-component 3.3 finances enhancement of institutional capacities of manage social protection programs in Somalia through establishment of Project Implementation Units.The BOOST-YOU project is processing additional financing (AF) under the Crisis Response Window (CRW) Early Response Financing (ERF) mechanism. The AF aims to help the Somali Government scale and enhance the project through three main components. Component 1, Connecting Youth and Women to Better Jobs Today, will be restructured to allow financial intermediation like the provision of microcredits, making it easier for young people involved in economic inclusion programs to access financial services. This will be implemented in partnership with Gargaara. Gargaara is an apex fund with a wholesale lending program providing microfinance services to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME). It was established with the assistance of the Somalia Productive, Resilient, and Inclusive Growth (SPRING) Project (P501662) and its predecessor Somalia Capacity Advancement, Livelihoods and Entrepreneurship, through Digital Uplift Project (SCALED-UP, P168115).Component 2, Investing in People for Better Jobs Tomorrow, will increase nutrition-linked Co-Responsibility Cash Transfers (CCTs). This expansion will support at least 83,000 households with pregnant women or children aged 0–2, especially those affected by climate-related shocks. Using data from the Unified Social Registry in targeted districts, this initiative is expected to reach about the poorest 54% of the population, in line with Somalia's national poverty line. As before, CCTs are intended to boost recipients resilience to climate challenges. This component will be implemented in collaboration with the health project (Improving Healthcare Services in Somalia Project (“Damal Caafimaad”) (P172031) with the implementing partner being UNICEF. Lastly, under Component 3, Adaptive Social Protection Systems and Project Management, additional resources will finance operational and capital needs. This includes setting up one-stop-shops within existing health facilities in target districts, as well as supporting oversight, management, and monitoring.
